claims.text: The initial material is a near-equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy.
Changing the percentage of individual elements in HfNbTaTiZr will systematically alter its mechanical properties.
Some constituent elements will contribute more strongly than others to strength and hardness.
Solid-solution strengthening is one mechanism by which elemental percentages affect strength and hardness.
Combinatorial sputtering or additive manufacturing can produce compositionally graded HfNbTaTiZr samples.
Localized mechanical characterization can correlate mechanical responses with local composition variations.
Spatial composition variation induces differences in grain-boundary characteristics.
Spatial composition variation induces differences in phase stability.
Spatial composition variation induces differences in defect density.
Changes in elemental percentages modify solid-solution strengthening.
Changes in elemental percentages may modify phase formation.
Modified solid-solution strengthening and phase formation affect local hardness and tensile strength.
Regions with adjusted elemental ratios will exhibit measurable mechanical-property differences relative to the near-equiatomic baseline.
Some elemental variations will produce a more pronounced strengthening effect than others.
Sample heterogeneity and experimental resolution may influence the measured magnitude and trend of mechanical-property changes.
Extreme composition deviations may cause phase transformations or other microstructural changes.
